sealed: Written and committed before the measurement code existed and before the pilot ran. pilot/measure.mjs refuses to run if this file differs from its commit, and the receipt names the commit. A claim that fails is kept as failed.
pilot: The Liveware Pilot: one real break-it node, as `node run.mjs` starts it, used as the secure ingest gateway for a partner's payment feed, measured end to end on the laptop that built it (Intel Core i7-1255U, Windows 11).

claims.claim: A real node admits all 180,000 payment records of the feed, in order. Not one genuine record is refused or lost.
claims.measure: the node's own count of admitted packets is 180,000; the ledger holds 180,000 entries; no genuine record got a refusal (a 429 rate-limit answer, if any, is retried and counted separately)

claims.claim: The books equal the feed exactly: for every one of the 30,000 accounts the posted balance is the sum of its six payments, and every account-month holds its own amount.
claims.measure: the node's /state compared key by key with the sums the feed kernel computes from the CSV alone

claims.claim: The node sustains at least 100 records a second over the whole feed on this laptop, with every record's signature checked and the record written to disk (fsync) before the app sees it.
claims.measure: 180,000 divided by the wall-clock seconds from the first record sent to the last answer received

claims.claim: The node process opens no outbound connection during the whole run: 0 TCP or TLS connects, 0 UDP sockets, 0 DNS lookups, 0 fetches.
claims.measure: hooks on net, tls, dgram, dns and fetch loaded into the node process before the node starts, read out at the end
the address the node's server reports it is bound to

claims.claim: Six known attack shapes injected mid-feed are each refused at the gate the first time and dropped on sight by an antibody the second time, and the feed around them is untouched: a replayed record, a record with one byte flipped, a record signed by a key that is not pinned, a record signed without the domain prefix, a truncated record, and an out-of-range record signed with the genuine key.
claims.measure: the node's answer to each injection, sent twice, byte for byte the same

claims.claim: The independent referee finds 0 breaches, and its fold of the ledger matches the app's state.
claims.measure: the node's /referee at the end of the run

claims.claim: The white-box red-team battery re-runs and reproduces its committed receipt byte for byte: 79 cases, every one held.

Every refusal the node makes carries a named stage and a plain-words reason, both in its HTTP answer and in its hash-chained journal; the ledger's hash chain verifies end to end, and its head can be re-derived offline from the feed alone.
claims.measure: every refusal answer and journal record checked for a stage from the gate's list and a reason in words; the ledger file re-loaded and its chain checked; its head compared with an offline derivation that signs the same 180,000 records without a node

computed_not_claimed: The CFO's cost case is arithmetic on sourced, dated list prices and the buyer's own figures (src/cost.mjs, gated), not a prediction, so it is not sealed here. Its one measured input, the records a second a node sustains, comes from claim coo-3.
